name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.IsSingletonIrreducibleModelAmongNonUnital
title: Singleton condition tested against all irreducible representations

content.display_title: Singleton condition tested against all irreducible representations
content.one_sentence_role: Defines the unital singleton condition while allowing the quantified representations to be presented without a unit equation.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a unital $*$-representation. The predicate below requires $\pi$ to be nonzero irreducible and compares it with every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho:A\to\mathcal B(K)$, even when the data type used for $\rho$ does not initially record $\rho(1_A)=I_K$.
content.definition_explanation: For every complete complex Hilbert space $K$ and every $*$-representation $\rho:A\to\mathcal B(K)$ that is nonzero irreducible, irreducibility forces $$\rho(1_A)=I_K.$$ Indeed, $\rho(1_A)$ is an idempotent whose range is a nonzero closed reducing subspace, hence all of $K$. The source expression `rho.toUnital hrho` therefore packages the same operator-valued map as a unital representation. The required conclusion is a unitary $U:H\to K$ satisfying $$U\pi(a)=\rho(a)U\qquad(a\in A).$$
content.assumptions: No separability or faithfulness assumption is included. The distinction is between a unital algebra and whether unit preservation is recorded in the representation interface; it is not a claim that $A$ or $\rho$ lacks a unit.
content.conclusion: The predicate says that $\pi$ represents the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations of the unital algebra $A$, with the same operator maps whether or not the input interface initially records the unit equation.
lean_realization_notes: The two implications in [Both directions of the singleton comparison](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/OrdinarySingleton.lean#L48-L76) identify this condition with the corresponding comparison restricted to unital representations: one direction regards the same unital representation through the interface that does not require a unit equation, the other uses the forced equation just proved. These remain distinct declared predicates and distinct Cards.
